title: `st.container` : Enable horizontal scrolling
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Containers today only enable a vertical scrolling of inner elements (widgets, or nested containers). Enabling horizontal behaviour would allow a lot of new interesting UI/UX patterns to emerge.

### Why?

There has been several occurences where I thought a horizontal container would work best, as a method to optimize the layout for complex ideas. For example, when developing a sort of workbench for a specific AI use case, where I want to build a lot of different purpose driven interfaces.

I feel that some basic but powerful layout options like horizontal scrolling is still what hinders from using streamlit has a SPA/App Platform when the use case gets richer.

### How?

Introduce the `direction` or `scrolling` parameter to `st.container` . I believe containers are the right place for layout options, since they can be nested into columns and combine to create very rich and intuitive horizontal and vertical layout options, without much cognitive load. 

### Additional Context

Today, creating something similar to this requires a lot of column nesting which in my experience is tough to make readable at all screen sizes, and is very annoying to develop for.

_No response_

comments.body:

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-9544)

Hey, thanks for the suggestion! We just started looking at new layout options, and indeed, one idea is to extend `st.container` as a basic building block for layout and turn it into something like a simplified flexbox. Haven't considered horizontal scrolling yet but will have a look!

## Update

Streamlit 1.63+ will allow to activate horizontal scrolling via `wrap=False`:

```python
with st.container(horizontal=True, wrap=False):
   ...
```
